facts.statement: The type species of the genus Nyana is Nyana rooiwalensis.
facts.quote: The type species is N. rooiwalensis.

facts.statement: Nyana lived during the Late Triassic Norian to Rhaetian ages.
The fossils of Nyana were found in the Elliot Formation of South Africa.
The fossil material of Nyana was discovered in 2018 in the lower Elliot Formation of Eastern Cape Province, South Africa.
facts.quote: The Nyana fossil material was discovered in 2018 in outcrops of the lower Elliot Formation in Eastern Cape Province, South Africa.

facts.statement: The generic name Nyana means "son" or "child" in Xhosa and "small" in Sesotho.
facts.quote: The generic name, Nyana, is a word meaning son or child in Xhosa, as well as small in Sesotho.

facts.statement: The specific epithet rooiwalensis refers to the locality Rooiwal where the specimen was found.
facts.quote: The specific name, rooiwalensis, references the discovery of the only known specimen in Rooiwal.

facts.statement: Nyana rooiwalensis was described in a 2026 Royal Society Open Science paper by Atashni Moopen and colleagues.
facts.quote: Year: 2026 Authors: Atashni Moopen, Jennifer Botha, Roger Benson, Kimberley E. J. Chapelle, Paul M. Barrett, Kathleen Dollman, Jonah N. Choiniere

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Nyana includes the braincase, palate, hyoid apparatus and scleral rings.
Body mass estimates suggest Nyana weighed about 400 kilograms.
Nyana provides the first well‑preserved near‑complete sauropodomorph skull from the lower Elliot Formation.
